Babylo.definition: Babylō ōnis, m a Babylonian, i. e. Nabob, T.

Bacchanal.definition: Bacchānal ālis, n Bacchus, a place dedicated to Bacchus, L.— Plur, the feast of Bacchus, revelries of Bacchus, L., C.: vivere, to live riotously, Iu.

Bacchus.definition: Bacchus ī, m, *ba/kxos, the son of Jupiter and Semele, the god of wine, of intoxication and inspiration.—Hence, the cry or invocation to Bacchus (Io Bacche!): audito Baccho, V.—The vine: Bacchus amat colles, V.: ferti…

Bactrius.definition: Bactrius adj., of Bactria (in Asia), O.

Baiae.definition: Bāiae (disyl.), ārum, f a watering-place in Campania: Baias iactare, i. e. luxurious holidays.

Bellona.definition: Bellōna ae, f bellum, the goddess of war, sister of Mars, L., V., H., O.

Bicorniger.definition: Bicorniger gerī, m bi-+corniger, the twohorned, i. e. Bacchus, O.

Bioneus.definition: Biōnēus adj. Bio, of Bion (a Greek philosopher), i. e. witty, satirical: sermones, H.

Bocchar.definition: 'Bocchar (-car) aris, m a king of Mauretania, L.: Cum Bocchare lavari, a Moor, Iu.'

Boeotius.definition: Boeōtius adj., Boeotian: moenia, of Thebes, O.

Boeotus.definition: Boeōtus adj., Boeotian: tellus, O.—Plur m. as subst, the Boeotians (proverbial for stupidity), L., H.

Bona1.definition: Bona dea the goddess of chastity and fertility, C., O., Iu.

Bosporus.definition: Bosporus ī, m, *bo/sporos heifer's ford, i. e. Io's passage; cf. Oxford. I. The strait of Constantinople, H.—II. (Sc. Cimmerius), the Cimmerian Bosporus, C., O., Pr.

Briseis.definition: Brīsēïs idos, f a daughter of Brises, i. e. Hippodamia, H.

Britannicus.definition: 'Britannicus adj., Britannic, British: aestus, the British Channel: lingua, Ta.: balaena, Iu.'

Britannus.definition: 'Britannus adj., of Britain: causidici, Iu.: esseda, Pr.'

Bromius.definition: Bromius ī, m, *bro/mios, a surname of Bacchus, O.

baca.definition: bāca (not bacca), ae, f a small round fruit, berry: bicolores, O.: lauri, V.: ebuli, V.: oleae, an olive: olivae, H.: bicolor Minervae, the olive, O.: bacae amarae, i. e. of the wild olive-tree, O.: silvestres, V. — A…

bacatus.definition: bācātus adj. baca, set with pearls, V.

baccaris.definition: baccaris (bacch-) aris, f, ba/kkaris, a plant whose root yielded a fragrant oil, V.

bacchabundus.definition: bacchābundus adj. bacchor, raving, riotous: agmen, Cu.

bacchantes.definition: bacchāntēs um, f P. of bacchor, bacchantes, priestesses of Bacchus: Bacchantum ritu, O.

bacchatio.definition: bacchātiō ōnis, f bacchor, plur, orgies, revelries: nocturnae.

bacchor.definition: bacchor ātus, ārī, dep. Bacchus, to celebrate the festival of Bacchus, rave like Bacchae, revel: quanta in voluptate, exult: in vestrā caede: non sanius Edonis, H.: per urbem, roams in frenzy, V.: Fama per urbem, runs…

bacifer.definition: bācifer fera, ferum, adj. baca + 1 FER-, bearing olives: Pallas, O.

bacillum.definition: bacillum ī, n dim. baculus, a wand, C.: dextram subiens, Iu.— Esp., a lictor's rod, C.

baculum.definition: baculum (or poet. baculus, m, O.), ī, n BA-, a stick, staff, walking-stick: baculo sustinet artūs, O.: baculo oculos alcui tundere: baculo innixus, O.: baculum quem lituum appellarunt, L.—A sceptre: aureum, Cu.

baiulo.definition: baiulō —, —, āre baiulus, to carry (of a heavy burden): sarcinas, Ph.

baiulus.definition: bāiulus ī, m a porter, carrier.

balaena.definition: bālaena (ball-) ae, f, fa/laina, a whale, O.

balans.definition: bālāns ntis, m and f P. of balo, a bleater, sheep (only plur; poet. for oves), V.

balanus.definition: balanus ī, f, ba/lanos (prop. an acorn; hence), a fragrant nut, ben-nut, H.

balatro.definition: balatrō ōnis, m a babbler, jester, buffoon, H.

balatus.definition: bālātus ūs, m balo, a bleating: Balatum exercere, V.: tener, O.: aegri, O.

balbus.definition: 'balbus adj. BAL-, BAR-, stammering, stuttering: Demosthenes: os, H.: verba, Tb.'

balbutio.definition: balbūtiō —, —, ire balbus, to stammer, stutter, speak childishly: perpauca: de naturā: illum Balbutit Scaurum (i. e. balbutiens appellat), H.

ballista.definition: ballista or bālista ae, f an engine for hurling: balistae emissiones lapidum habent: asseres ballistis missi, Cs.: porta ballistis instructa, L.

balnearius.definition: balneārius adj. balneum, of baths, at baths: fur, Ct.—Plur n. as subst, a bath, bath-room.

balneator.definition: balneātor ōris, m balneum, a bath-keeper.

balneolum.definition: balneolum ī, n dim. balneum, a small bath, Iu.

balo.definition: bālō āvī, —, āre BAL-, BAR-, to bleat, O.: balantes hostiae, i. e. oves, Enn. ap. C.: pecus balans, Iu.

balsamum.definition: balsamum ī, n, ba/lsamon, the balsam-tree: balsami umor, Ta.— Plur, a fragrant gum, balsam, V., Ta.

baltea.definition: baltea ōrum, n cf. Engl. belt, a girdle, belt, sword-belt, shoulder-band, baldric: auro caelatus, O.: (pharetram) circumplectitur auro Balteus, a quiver-belt, V.: verutum in balteo defigitur, Cs.: quotiens rumoribus u…

barathrum.definition: barathrum ī, n, ba/rathron, an abyss, chasm, gulf, pit:v inmane, V.: imus barathri gurges, V.: barathro donare alqd, i. e. throw away, H.— Of a greedy man: barathrum macelli, an abyss of the butcher's stall, H.

barba.definition: barba ae, f Engl. beard, the beard: promissa, long, L.: inpexae barbae, V.: prima, Iu.: barbam tondere: ponere, H.: metire, Iu.: recidere, O.: submittere, Ta.: barbam vellere alicui, to pluck one by the beard, H.: sap…

barbare.definition: barbarē adv. barbarus, rudely, incorrectly: loqui.—Roughly, cruelly: Laedens oscula, H.

barbaria.definition: barbaria ae (nom. also -iēs, acc. iem), f barbarus, a strange land, foreign country (opp. Greece and Italy): barbariae bellum inferre: Quid tibi barbariem ... numerem? O.: Graecia barbariae conlisa, i. e. Phrygia, H.:…

barbaricus.definition: barbaricus adj., foreign, strange: supellex, L.: astante ope barbaricā , Eastern, Enn. ap. C.: ope barbaricā Victor, with Eastern hordes, V.

barbarismus.definition: barbarismus ī, m, barbarismo/s, an impropriety of speech, barbarism, Her.

barbarus.definition: barbarus adj. with (poet.) comp., ba/rbaros, of strange speech, speaking jargon, unintelligible: lingua, S.: sum, quia non intellegor ulli, O. — Foreign, strange, barbarous, uncivilized, not Greek nor Roman: mixta Gra…

barbatulus.definition: barbātulus adj. dim. barbatus, with a small beard: mulli: iuvenes, i. e. foppish.

barbatus.definition: barbātus adj. barba, having a beard, bearded: Iuppiter: hirculus, Ct.: equitare Si quem delectet barbatum, a grown man, H.: nondum, i. e. while a boy, Iu.: bene unus ex barbatis illis, i. e. the old Romans (who wore f…

barbitos.definition: barbitos ī, m a lyre, lute: dic Latinum, Barbite, Carmen, H.

barbula.definition: barbula ae, f dim. barba, a little beard.

barditus.definition: bardītus or barītus (barr-) ī, m the warsong of the Germans, Ta.

baris.definition: bāris idos, f, ba=ris, a small row-boat, Pr.

baro.definition: bārō ōnis, m a simpleton, blockhead.

barrus.definition: barrus ī, m Indian, an elephant, H.

bascauda.definition: bascauda ae, f cf. Engl. basket, a woven mat, dish holder of basket-work, Iu.

basiatio.definition: bāsiātiō ōnis, f basio, a kissing, kiss, Ct.

basilica.definition: 'basilica ae, f, basilikh/ (sc. stoa/), a portico, basilica; in Rome, a public building used for a merchants'' exchange and for the courts, basilica: basilicas spoliis ornare: neque enim tum basilicae erant (B.C. 212)…

basio.definition: bāsiō āvī, atus, āre basium, to kiss: oculos, Ct.: alqm multa basia, Ct.

basis.definition: basis is, f, ba/sis, a foundation, base, support, pedestal, villae: (statuā ) abiectā basim manere: Sc<*>pionis, i. e. of his statue. — A base: trianguli.

basium.definition: bāsium ī, n a kiss: da mi basia mille, Ct.: basia iactare, to throw kisses of the hand, Ph., Iu.

batillum.definition: batillum (vatillum) ī, m dim, a fire - pan, chafing-dish: prunae, H.

beate.definition: beātē adv. beatus, happily: vivere: est mihi bene ac beate, quod, etc., Ct.

beatum.definition: beātum ī, n beatus, happiness, felicity.

beatus.definition: beātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of beo, happy, prosperous, blessed, fortunate: beatus, ni unum hoc desit, T.: Beatus ille, qui, etc., H.: nihil est ab omni Parte beatum, H.: beatissima vita: res p., L.: quo beatus …

bellator.definition: bellātor ōris, m bello, a warrior, soldier, fighting man: de re p.: primus, L.—Esp. in apposition for an adj., warlike, ready to fight, martial, valorous: bellator Turnus, V.: deus, the war-god Mars, V.: equus, spirit…

bellatrix.definition: bellātrīx īcis, f bellator, a female warrior; freq. in apposition for an adj., warlike, skilled in war, serviceable in war: Penthesilea, V.: Minerva, O.: bellatrix iracundia, warlike rage.

belle.definition: bellē adv. with sup. bellus, prettily, neatly, well: belle et festive (in applause): se habere, to be well: minus belle habere, to be not quite well: bellissime esse: hoc non belle, a fault, H.: cum hoc fieri bellissi…

bellicosus.definition: bellicōsus adj. with comp. and sup. bellicus, warlike, martial, valorous, given to fighting: gentes: bellicosissimae nationes: naturā gens, S.: provinciae, Cs.: quod bellicosius fuerit, would have been a greater achie…

bellicum.definition: bellicum ī, n bellicus, the war - trumpet, war-signal; only with canere, to call to arms, signal for the onset: motus novus bellicum canere coepit: bellicum me cecinisse dicunt, began hostilities.—Of style: canere quo…

bellicus.definition: bellicus adj. bellum, of war, military: bellicam rem administrare: disciplina: laus, military glory, Cs.: caerimoniae, L.: casūs, the chances of war: tubicen, O.: naves, Pr. — Warlike, fierce in war: Pallas, O.: virgo…

belliger.definition: 'belliger era, erum, adj. bellum + GES-, warlike, martial, belligerent: ensis, O.: gentes, O.'

belligero.definition: belligerō —, ātus, āre belliger, to carry on war, wage war: nec cauponantes bellum, sed belligerantes, i. e. in earnest, Enn. ap. C.: cum fortuna: tumultuatum verius quam belligeratum, L.

bellipotens.definition: bellipotēns ntis, adj. bellum + potens, mighty in battle, Enn. ap. C.—Subst., i. e. Mars, V.

bello.definition: bellō āvī, ātum, āre bellum, to wage war, carry on war, war: cum Aetolis: adversum patrem, N.: pro Samnitibus adversus Romanos, L.: ad bellandum profecti, Ta.: bellum a consulibus bellatum, conducted, L.: cum muliercu…

bellor.definition: bellor —, ārī, dep., to war, fight (rare for bello): pictis armis, V.

bellum.definition: bellum old and poet. duellum, ī, n DVA-, DVI-, war. — Form duellum: agere rem duelli, C. (lex): purum piumque, L. (old record): victoria duelli, L. (oracle): Pacem duello miscuit, H. — Form bellum: Germanicum, against…

bellus.definition: bellus adj. with sup dim. for *bonulus, from bonus.—Of persons, pretty, handsome, neat, pleasant, fine, agreeable: puella bellissima: fac bellus revertare, in good spirits: homines, gentlemen.— Of things, choice, fine…

belua.definition: bēlua (not bellua), ae, f a beast, wild beast, monster: fera: saeva, H.: Lernae, the Hydra, V.: in usu beluarum: quantum natura hominis pecudes reliquaque belua, lower animals. — Esp., the elephant, T.: beluarum manūs…

beluosus.definition: bēluōsus adj. belua, abounding in monsters: Oceanus, H.

bene2.definition: bene dīcō, bene dictum, bene faciō, bene factum see bene.

beneficentia.definition: beneficentia ae, f beneficus, kindness, practical good-will, philanthropy: quid praestantius beneficentiā?: adversus supplices, Ta.

beneficiarii.definition: beneficiāriī ōrum, m beneficium, soldiers exempt from common labor, a body-guard, Cs.

beneficium.definition: beneficium ī, n bene+2 FAC-, a favor, benefit, service, kindness: Pro maleficio beneficium reddere, T.: alcui dare: apud bonos beneficium conlocare, lay under obligation: Iugurtham beneficiis vincere, S.: in regem: er…

beneficus.definition: 'beneficus (not benif-), adj. with sup. bene+ 2 FAC-, generous, liberal, serviceable, beneficent, bountiful: viri: in amicum: voluntas: ut ii sint beneficentissimi.'

benevole.definition: benevolē (not beniv-), adv. benevolus, kindly: fieri: praesto esse alcui.

benevolens.definition: benevolēns ntis, adj. with comp. and sup, friendly, kind: illi benevolens, T.: benevolentior tibi: officium benevolentissimi.

benevolentia.definition: benevolentia (not beniv-), ae, f benevolus, good-will, benevolence, kindness, favor, friendship: ad benevolentiam coniungendam: benevolentiam capere: animos ad benevolentiam adlicere: alqm benevolentiā complecti: quae…

benevolus.definition: benevolus (not beniv-), adj. bene+1 VOL-, well-wishing, kind, bountiful, friendly: alcui esse: animus: servi, devoted. — For comp. and sup., see benevolens.

benigne.definition: benīgnē adv. with comp. and sup. benignus, in a friendly manner, kindly, benevolently, courteously, benignly: facere, T.: viam monstrare, courteously: audire: respondere, S.: adloqui, L.: arma capere, cheerfully, L.: …

benignitas.definition: benīgnitās ātis,f benignus, kindness, friendliness, courtesy, benevolence, benignity: me summā cum benignitate auditis: benignitate adducti alqd concedere: deūm, L.—Kindness, liberality, bounty, favor: ubi meam Benign…

benignus.definition: benīgnus adj. with comp. bene+GEN-, kind, good, friendly, pleasing, favorable, benignant: animus in alqm, T.: numen, H.: oratio: benigniora verba, L. — Beneficent, obliging, liberal, bounteous: fortuna mihi, H.: benig…

beo.definition: beō āvī, ātus, āre cf. bonus, to make happy, gladden, bless: te, gratify, T.: caelo Musa beat, rewards, H.: Munere te, H.: Latium divite linguā, H.: O factum bene, beasti, I am delighted, T.

berullos.definition: bērullos (bēryl-) ī, m,=bh/rullos, the beryl, <*>u.— A ring with a beryl, Pr.

bes.definition: bēs bēssis, m for * bi-assi-s, two thirds: fends factum bessibus, i. e. at two thirds of an as per hundred each month, eight per cent. per annum.

bestia.definition: bēstia ae, f a beast, animal: fera bestia, N.: tametsi bestiae sunt (canes): bestiae volucres, birds: mutae, L.: ad bestias mittere alqm, to fight with (in the public spectacles): mala, the odor of the armpits (cf. ca…

bestiarius.definition: bēstiārius ī, m bestia, one who fights with wild beasts (in the shows): ducenti.

bestiola.definition: bēstiola ae, f dim. bestia, a small animal, little living creature.

beta1.definition: bēta ae, f a beet (a vegetable), C., Ct.

beta2.definition: bēta n indecl, the Greek letter B, Iu.

bi-.definition: bi- praep insep. DVA-, twice, double.

bibliotheca.definition: bibliothēca ae (rarely Gr. acc. -ēcēn, C.), f, bibliothh/kh, a library, room for books: abdo me in bibliothecam.—A library, collection of books.

bibo.definition: bibō bibī, —, ere BI-, to drink: vinum, T.: mella diluta, H.: lac, to suck, O.: gemmā, from a jewelled cup, V.: caelato (sc. poculo), Iu.: Quod iussi ei dari bibere, to be given her to drink, T.: ut bibere sibi iubere…

bibulus.definition: bibulus adj. bibo, given to drink, drinking freely: potores, H.: Falerni, H. — Of things, absorbent, thirsty: harena, V.: lapis, V.: talaria, moistened, O.: bibulas tinguebat murice lanas, O.

biceps.definition: 'biceps cipitis, adj. bi- + caput, with two heads, two-headed: puella: Ianus, O.: partus, Ta.: Parnasus, with two summits. O.'

bicolor.definition: bicolor ōris, adj. bi-+color, of two colors, two-colored: equus, V.: baca, O.

bicornis.definition: 'bicornis e, adj. bi-+cornu, with two horns, two - horned: caper, O.: fauni, O.: furcae, twopronged, V.: luna, i. e. the new moon, H.: Rhenus, with two mouths, V.'

bicorpor.definition: bicorpor oris, adj. bis- + corpus, of two bodies: manus, of a centaur, C. poët.

bidens.definition: bidēns entis (abl. entī or ente; gen plur. entium or entum), adj. bi-+dens, with two teeth: forfex, two - bladed, V.—As subst m., a heavy hoe, mattock with two iron teeth: glaebam frangere bidentibus, V.: bidentis ama…

bidental.definition: bidental ālis, n bidens, a place struck by lightning (consecrated by a sacrifice): triste, H.

biduum.definition: bīduum ī, n bi-+dies, a period of two days, two days: concedere, T.: biduist Haec sollicitudo, is a matter of, T.: omnino biduum supererat, remained, Cs.: eximere biduum ex mense: biduum cibo se abstinere, N.: supplic…

biennium.definition: biennium ī, n bi-+annus, a period of two years, two years: per biennium: ad alqd biennium sibi satis esse, Cs.: provinciam obtinere, for two years: comitia biennio habita, in the last two years, L.: post biennium, aft…

bifariam.definition: bifārīam adv. bi-+1 FA-, on two sides, i. e. twofold, double, in two ways, in two parts, in two places, severally: divisis copiis, L.: aequaliter distributa: ingressi hostium fines, L.: gemina victoria duobus bifariam…

bifer.definition: 'bifer era, erum, adj. bi-+1 FER-, bearing twice: biferi rosaria Paesti, blooming twice a year, V.'

bifidus.definition: 'bifidus adj. bi-+2 FID-, cleft, parted, split: pedes, O.'

biforis.definition: 'biforis e, adj. bi- + foris, with two doors, folding: valvae, O.: cantus (tibiae), i. e. of the double tibia, V.'

biformatus.definition: bi-fōrmātus adj., of two forms, double: impetus, C. (poet.).

biformis.definition: bifōrmis e, adj. bi-+forma, of double form, two-formed, two-shaped: Minotaurus, V.: Ianus, O.: pater, i. e. Chiron, O.—Fig., of a poet.: vates, H.

bifrons.definition: bi-frōns ontis, adj., with two foreheads, with two faces: Ianus, V.

bifurcus.definition: 'bifurcus adj. bi-+furca, having two prongs, two-pronged: ramus, two-forked, O.: valli, L.'

bigae.definition: bīgae ārum, f for biiugae, a span of horses, pair, two horses harnessed to an open car: raptatus bigis, V.: bigis in albis, with white horses, V.: citae, Ct.—Sing: habenae bigae, Ta.

bigatus.definition: bīgātus adj. bigae, bearing the figure of a two-horse car: argentum, L.—Hence, as subst, a silver coin stamped with a harnessed span of horses: quingenti, L., Ta.

biiugis.definition: biiugis e, adj. bi- + iugum, yoked two together: equi, V.: biiugūm Colla lyncūm, O.

biiugus.definition: biiugus adj. bi-+iugum, yoked two together: leones, V.: certamen, a chariot-race, V.—Plur. as subst m. (sc. equi), two horses yoked abreast: telo Admonuit biiugos, V.: desiluit biiugis, i. e. from his chariot, V.

bilibra.definition: bi-lībra ae, f two pounds: bilibris farris emisse, for two pounds of corn each, L.

bilibris.definition: bilībris e, adj. bilibra, of two pounds; hence, cornu, holding two pints, H.

bilinguis.definition: bilinguis e, adj. bi-+lingua, two - tongued, speaking a jumble of languages: Canusini more, H. —Fig., double-tongued, hypocritical, false: Tyrii, V.

bilis.definition: bīlis is, abl. lī or le, f bile: aut pituita aut bilis: purgor bilem, H.—Fig., anger, wrath, choler, indignation: bilem commovere: mihi Bilem movere, H.: bile tumet iecur, H.: splendida, H.: bilem effundere, to vent, …

bilix.definition: bilīx īcis, adj. bi-+LAC-, LIC-, with a double thread: lorica, V.

bilustris.definition: bilūstris e, adj. bi-+lustrum, that lasts ten years: bellum, O.

bimaris.definition: 'bi-maris e, adj., between two seas: Corinthus, H.: Isthmos, O.'

bimaritus.definition: bi-marītus ī, m the husband of two wives, a bigamist (once).

bimater.definition: (bi-māter tris), adj., having two mothers (only acc sing.), of Bacchus, O.

bimembris.definition: bimembris e, adj. bi- + membrum, with double members: puer, half man, half beast, Iu.— Of the Centaurs: forma, O. — Plur m. as subst, the Centaurs: nubigenae, V.: germani, O.

bimestris.definition: bimēstris e, adj. bi-+mensis, of two months: stipendium, L.: porcus, two months old, H.

bimulus.definition: bīmulus adj. dim. bimus, only two years old: puer, Ct.

bimus.definition: bīmus adj. bi-+hiems, of two winters, of two years, two years old: merum, H.: honos, O.: sententia, a commission for two years, Planc. ap. C.

bini.definition: bīnī ae, a (gen. bīnūm), num distr. DVA-, two by two, two to each, two each, two at a time: ex praediis talenta bina, every year two talents, T.: censores binos in singulas civitates: si unicuique bini pedes adsignent…

binoctium.definition: binoctium ī, n bi- + nox, a space of two nights, Ta.

binominis.definition: (binōminis e),adj. bi-+nomen, bearing two names, only gen sing.: Ascanius, O.

bipalmis.definition: 'bipalmis e, adj. bi-+palmus, two spans long: spiculum, L.'

bipartito.definition: bipartītō or bipertītō adv. bipartitus, in two parts, in two divisions, in two ways: classem distribuere: signa inferre, to attack in two divisions, Cs.: equites emissi, L.: ita bipartito fuerunt ut Tiberis interesset.

bipatens.definition: bi-patēns adj., with double opening: portae, folding, V.: tecta, with doors on both sides, V.

bipedalis.definition: bi-pedālis is, adj., of two feet, measuring two feet: trabes, two feet thick, Cs.: modulus, two feet long, H.

bipennifer.definition: 'bipennifer era, erum, adj. bipennis + 1 FER-, bearing a two-edged axe: Lycurgus, O.'

bipennis.definition: bipennis e, adj. bi-+penna, with two edges, two-edged: ferrum, V. — As subst f. (sc. securis), with acc. em (once -im, O.), abl. ī (once e, Tb.), a two-edged axe, double axe, battle-axe: correptā bipenni, V.: lata, O.…

bipes.definition: bi-pēs pedis, adj., two-footed, biped: equi, V.: asellus, Iu.—Plur m. as subst, bipeds, men.

biremis.definition: birēmis e, adj. bi-+remus, with two oars, two-oared: scapha, H.— With two banks of oars: lembi, L.—As subst f., a galley with two banks of oars: biremes impulsae vectibus, Cs.: Phrygiae, V.

bis.definition: bis adv. num. DVA-, DVI-, twice, at two times, on two occasions: non semel sed bis: bis ac saepius, N.: bis mori, H.: bis consul, twice a consul: a te bis terve (litteras) accepi, two or three times: Quem bis terve bo…

bisulcus.definition: 'bi-sulcus adj., having two furrows, forked, cloven: lingua, O.: pes, O.'

bitumen.definition: bitūmen inis, n mineral pitch, bitumen: nigrum, V., H.: tenax, O.

bitumineus.definition: bitūmineus adj. bitumen, of bitumen: vires, O.

bivius.definition: bivius adj. bi-+via, of two ways, having two approaches: fauces, V.— As subst n., a place where two roads meet: portae, the fork at the gate, V.: ad bivia consistere, L.
